item.title: Sanctuary for Chonky Felines Helps Surrendered Obese Cat Lose Weight
item.description: Kristine of The Big House Cats sanctuary in Ottawa shared the incredible story of CC, a 23-pound cat who was surrendered due to her weight.

item.title: Artist Carves Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics Into Solid Stone Using a Mallet and Chisel
item.description: Stonemason Miriam Johnson used a mallet and chisel to show how Ancient Egyptians carved hieroglyphics into solid stone.

item.title: How the Darién Gap Prevents the Pan-American Highway From Becoming the World’s Longest Road
item.description: Map Men explained how the Pan American Highway is interrupted by the Darién Gap, an impassable rainforest between Panama and Colombia.

item.title: How a 1980s Synthesizer Patch Created the Legendary 'Hoover Sound' of 1990s Raves
item.description: "Mixed Signals" explained how the “What The?” patch on the Roland Alpha Juno in the 80s became the preeminent "Hoover" sound of the 1990s.

item.title: Why Modern Canned Food Doesn’t Spoil Over Time
item.description: "Simple Things – Surprising Histories" explained why modern canned food doesn't spoil due to pressure cooking and vacuum sealing.

item.title: A Bipedal Robot That Inline Skates, Climbs Stairs, and Balances on One Wheel
item.description: RAI Institute built the "Roadrunner", an autonomous bipedal robot prototype that can skate, climb stairs, and balance on one wheel.

item.title: XenoFrog – A Clever Kermit the Frog and 'Alien' Xenomorph Mashup Sculpture
item.description: Ed Harrington partnered with Mark Pendley to turn his Kermit the Frog and Xenomorph mashup sketch "XenoFrog" into a premium resin sculpture.

item.title: The Tallest Building in Every US State
item.description: Ken from "This House" virtually toured the United States in alphabetical order, noting the tallest buildings in each state.

item.title: Marine Biologist Spends 92 Days Removing Hundreds of Deadly Barnacles From a Debilitated Turtle
item.description: Marine biologist Tabitha Siegfried spent 92 days removing barnacles from a turtle who had a severe case of Debilitated Turtle Syndrome.

item.title: What Happens Inside Your Body When You Eat a 'Do Not Eat' Silica Gel Packet
item.description: A TED-Ed lesson written by Vivian Jiang explains what happens to the human body when the little "do not eat" silica gel packets are eaten.

item.title: How a 1960s British 'Cowboy' Instrumental Became a Staple of Early New York City Hip-Hop
item.description: "Mixed Signals" looked at how the British "cowboy" instrumental "Apache" went to become a staple of early New York City hip hop.

item.title: How Language Influences the Way We Visualize Time
item.description: Dr. Erica Brozovsky of "Otherwords" explains how the visualization of time depends on the language being spoken.

item.title: How Green Became the Standard Color for Circuit Boards
item.description: "Simple Things – Surprising Histories" looked at circuit boards to find out why most of them are a particular shade of green.

item.title: Water Loving Cat Waits Impatiently in the Tub for His Monthly Bath Time
item.description: A hydrophilic cat named Ash loves his monthly bath time so much that he waits impatiently in the tub for his human to turn on the water.

item.title: A Multi-Layered Mashup of Queen’s ‘Fat Bottomed Girls’ and ‘Tubthumping’ by Chumbawamba
item.description: DJ Cummerbund combined the classic Queen song "Fat Bottom Girls" with songs by various artists to create a seamless, multi-layered mashup.
